title: Weep Thou, O Mourner! but in Lamentation
description: Weep Thou, O Mourner! but in Lamentation in Tonic Solfa to PERFECT LOVE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 340, “The Mourner”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Elevens and Tens (11.10.11.10) (11.10.11.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PERFECT LOVE; any other Elevens and Tens (11.10.11.10) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Weep thou, O mourn-er! but in la-men-ta-tion Let thy Re-deem-er still re-mem-bered be; Strong is His arm, the God of thy sal-va-tion, Strong is His love to cheer and com-fort thee.

lines: Weep thou, O mourner! but in lamentation
Let thy Redeemer still remembered be;
Strong is His arm, the God of thy salvation,
Strong is His love to cheer and comfort thee.
Cold though the world be, in the way before thee
Wail not in sadness o'er the darkling tomb;
God in His love still watcheth kindly o'er thee,
Light shineth still above the clouds of gloom.
Dimmed though thine eyes be with the tears of sorrow
Night only known beneath the sky of time,
Faith can behold the dawning of a morrow
Glowing in smiles of life and joy sublime.
Change, then, O mourner, grief to exultation;
Firm and confiding should thy spirit be;
Strong is His arm, the God of thy salvation,
Strong is His love to cheer and comfort thee.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to PERFECT LOVE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
